records.title: EpiCache: Episodic KV Cache Management for Long-Term Conversation on Resource-Constrained Environments
records.reason: EpiCache is a training-free KV management framework for long-term LLM conversation. It processes history in blocks, evicts less critical entries as it prefills, clusters context into episodes and allocates cache according to episodic relevance and sensitivity, bounding peak KV memory instead of first materializing the full context. It evaluates multi-turn conversational QA on RealTalk, LoCoMo and LongMemEval under resource limits. The work directly addresses inference-time memory and long-context processing.

records.title: FastMTP: Accelerating LLM Inference with Enhanced Multi-Token Prediction
records.reason: FastMTP adapts multi-token prediction for speculative decoding at inference time, improving multi-step draft quality and reducing draft computation with language-aware vocabulary compression. Across seven benchmarks, the paper reports average 2.03x speedup versus standard next-token prediction with lossless output quality and 82% gain over vanilla MTP. The conclusion describes the work as inference acceleration.

records.title: InfLLM-V2: Dense-Sparse Switchable Attention for Seamless Short-to-Long Adaptation
records.reason: InfLLM-V2 adds a dense-sparse switchable attention framework for long-context LLM inference. It uses sparse attention for long inputs while retaining dense behavior for shorter contexts, and reduces the overhead of its compression attention. The paper reports 4× speed over dense attention with 98.1% and 99.7% retained performance on its long-context and chain-of-thought evaluations; its end-to-end 8B experiment reports 2.13× prefill and 2.32× decode speedups in the stated setting. This directly targets attention compute and inference latency.

records.title: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems
records.reason: Speculative Actions accelerates general agentic systems by predicting and executing likely future API actions in parallel, with LLM calls among a broader set of tool/MCP/human actions. Its evaluations cover gaming, e-commerce, web search and an OS setting, reporting up to 20% latency reduction, but do not isolate LLM inference latency or serving throughput. Retained as borderline because it includes LLM-agent loops while its objective/evaluation extends well beyond LLM inference.

records.title: When to Reason: Semantic Router for vLLM
records.reason: The semantic router predicts whether a query benefits from reasoning and selects reasoning or direct inference accordingly, avoiding unnecessary inference-time token generation for simple prompts. Against direct inference with vLLM, the paper reports +10.2 percentage points on MMLU-Pro while reducing response latency by 47.1% and token use by 48.5%; it reports robust gains across 11 of 14 domains, with weaker results in reasoning-heavy areas. This directly optimizes inference cost and latency.

records.title: KVCOMM: Online Cross-context KV-cache Communication for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
records.reason: KVCOMM communicates reusable KV states online across agents with overlapping contexts and aligns tokens that occur at different offsets. Reported cases include more than 70% reuse and, for one three-agent H100 setting, 6.7x average prefill speedup; the paper also reports 95% reuse on GSM8K over 1,319 samples with less than 2.5% accuracy drop. Limitations include homogeneous text agents, no decode-latency evaluation, and future work for dynamic/heterogeneous settings.

records.title: SpecDiff-2: Scaling Diffusion Drafter Alignment For Faster Speculative Decoding
records.reason: SpecDiff-2 improves diffusion-based speculative decoding by aligning a larger diffusion drafter to the target's accepted token streaks. Its experiments report an average 4.22× speedup across settings and more than 30% over EAGLE-2; on structured reasoning/code workloads the speedups are strongest, and a fixed wall-time Math500 evaluation shows the increased decoding throughput can improve answer accuracy under a time budget. Training the drafter is part of the method, but the paper's stated outcome is inference acceleration.

records.title: ContextPilot: Fast Long-Context Inference via Context Reuse
records.reason: ContextPilot aligns and deduplicates context blocks to increase prefix KV-cache reuse and accelerate long-context prefill. Across stated RAG workloads it reports 1.5–3× throughput over named systems with negligible accuracy loss; it reports up to 3.1× prefill-throughput improvement in its evaluation and latency reductions on consumer devices. Direct inference prefill optimization.

records.title: Pre-Attention Expert Prediction and Prefetching for Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models
records.reason: A same-layer pre-attention predictor prefetches MoE experts while attention runs. The paper reports exact-match prediction rates of 93.03% for DeepSeek-V2-Lite, 94.69% for Qwen3-30B, and 97.62% for Phi-mini, with expected expert-load delay reduced to 0.27-0.64 ms/token versus FATE's 0.85-2.01 ms/token. It notes that end-to-end system integration remains future work, but the evaluated method directly targets inference prefetch latency.

records.title: T-SAR: A Full-Stack Co-design for CPU-Only Ternary LLM Inference via In-Place SIMD ALU Reorganization
records.reason: T-SAR is a full-stack CPU-only ternary LLM inference design. It reports 5.6-24.5x GEMM-latency and 1.1-86.2x GEMV-throughput improvements, and up to 2.5-4.9x energy efficiency over Jetson AGX Orin. The full evaluation shows platform-specific tradeoffs: on mobile CPU decode throughput is lower than Jetson despite lower energy/token. This directly addresses efficient LLM inference on edge CPUs.

records.title: MatKV: Trading Compute for Flash Storage in LLM Inference
records.reason: MatKV caches document KV on flash to avoid recomputing repeated RAG prefill. In the stated batched LLaMA 3.1 70B experiment it reports up to 2× prefill speedup; for overlapped SSD KV loading and GPU decoding it reports up to 2× inference speedup. This directly targets inference latency and cost. The paper notes selective materialization as future work, so break-even assumptions matter.

records.title: Nalar: A Serving Framework for Agent Workflows
records.reason: Nalar is explicitly an LLM-agent serving framework with adaptive scheduling, routing, resource management and state placement. In end-to-end workflow experiments it reports P95/P99 latency reductions of roughly 34%-74%; at 8 requests/s, P99 is about 3.75x lower, while average-latency improvements are more modest (8%-35%). The paper also evaluates policy control and scalability using profiled LLM inference. This directly studies serving efficiency for agentic LLM workflows.

records.title: Double: Breaking the Acceleration Limit via Double Retrieval Speculative Parallelism
records.reason: Double combines iterative draft-side retrieval with target-side retrieval guidance to avoid speculative-decoding speed ceilings and recover from early mismatches. It is training-free and lossless; the paper reports 5.3x speedup on Llama 3.3 70B and 2.8x on Qwen3 32B, including 5.3x against EAGLE-3. This directly accelerates LLM decoding.

records.title: Fast KVzip: Efficient and Accurate LLM Inference with Gated KV Eviction
records.reason: Fast KVzip uses lightweight sink-attention gates to retain important KV pairs during prefill and decoding, targeting frozen-weight inference while eliminating runtime compression overhead. Across Qwen2.5-1M, Qwen3 and Gemma3, it reports reducing KV-cache size to 30% with negligible performance loss across long-context, code, retrieval and reasoning tasks. This directly reduces inference memory requirements.

records.title: ScaleSim: Serving Large-Scale Multi-Agent Simulation with Invocation Distance-Based Memory Management
records.reason: The worklist row has only the arXiv identifier as its title; the primary arXiv paper identifies itself as ScaleSim. It targets GPU memory pressure in LLM-based multi-agent simulation and implements invocation-distance-guided proactive prefetch and priority-based eviction for LLM serving. Across three simulation workloads it reports up to 1.74× speedup over a vanilla SGLang baseline. This directly optimizes LLM serving for agent workloads.

records.title: ProphetKV: User-Query-Driven Selective Recomputation for Efficient KV Cache Reuse in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
records.reason: ProphetKV targets long-context RAG prefill. It reuses precomputed KV for retrieved chunks and selectively recomputes query-relevant tokens to recover important cross-attention information that blind KV reuse loses. The method is designed to retain high accuracy close to full recomputation while reducing the repeated prefill computation. This is directly an inference-time KV reuse and prefill efficiency method.

records.title: HySparse: A Hybrid Sparse Attention Architecture with Oracle Token Selection and KV Cache Sharing
records.reason: HySparse interleaves full-attention and sparse-attention layers, using full attention as an oracle for token selection and sharing KV cache across sparse layers to reduce both computation and memory. It evaluates dense 7B and MoE 80B models; in the 80B case only 5 of 49 layers use full attention while KV storage is reduced nearly 10x. This directly targets efficient long-context LLM inference.
